subject: Strange behaviour of scale parameters in a linear mixed-effects model

messages.author: 448099c49d2e6054
messages.subject: Strange behaviour of scale parameters in a linear mixed-effects model
parts:
Hi all,

I'm using a linear mixed-effects model to compare two measurement systems (shown below). The data contains the measurements, y, which are indexed in database form by: item (item), measurement method (meth), replicate index (repl), and an item-replicate index (repl_ind).

This is basically a Stan (Rstan) implementation of the model proposed by Cartensen et al., whereby we are including explicit random effects to model the replicate structure of our data. Note that we have an unbalanced replicate design, with a large number of items having between 1 and 3 replicates, a smaller number between 4 and 6 replicates, and one item has 7 replicates.

As recommended, I have used non-centred parameterisation for the individual effects and boundary avoiding Gamma priors on the variance components. However, I am encountering some issues. Firstly, it appears that, in general, the sigma parameters in the model behave rather strangely. We ran the model with 4 chains and 10,000 iterations (5,000 warmup) which produced output as included in the attachments (model_orig.txt, model_orig_small.pdf). The sigma[1] parameter appears to be exploring a realistic parameter space, but clearly not in the best way. Likewise the sigma[2] parameter exhibits some mixing issues. Furthermore, we encounter treedepth issues and divergent transitions with this model. Therefore, we increased adapt_delta from 0.8 to 0.9, and increased max_treedepth from 10 to 15. This appears to do away with treedepth issues but the many divergent transitions remain. Further, modifying the tuning parameters seems to do little to improve chain mixing for our problematic parameters (model_orig_tuned.txt, model_orig_tuned_small.pdf).

We ran the same models on other, similar data (with y of a different magnitude) and saw similar behaviour.

Does anyone have any insight into what could be going wrong and/or suggestions for model improvement?

Cheers,

Rob

data {

    int<lower=0>                n_all;
    int<lower=0>               n_item;
    int<lower=0>               n_meth;
    int<lower=0>               n_repl;
    real                     y[n_all];  // outcome variable
    int<lower=1>          item[n_all];  // item index
    int<lower=1>          meth[n_all];  // method index
    int<lower=1>          repl[n_all];  // replicate index
    int<lower=1>      repl_ind[n_all];  // item-replicate index
}

transformed data {

    int<lower=1> n_factor;
    n_factor   <- n_all/2;

}

parameters {

    // Parameters for each method.
    vector[n_meth] alpha;  // mean effect
    vector[n_meth] sigma;  // sd

    // Random effects due to item.
    vector[n_item]     u_raw;  // per-item random effect
    real<lower=0>      gamma;  // sd

    // Random effects due to interaction between items and methods.
    vector[n_item]   c_raw[n_meth];  // per-combination random effect
    real<lower=0>              tau;  // sd

    // Random effects due to interaction between items and replicates.
    vector[n_factor]   a_raw;  // item-replicate interaction effect
    real<lower=0>      omega;  // sd


}

model {
    vector[n_item]           u;  // per-item random effect
    vector[n_item]   c[n_meth];  // per-combination random effect
    vector[n_factor]         a;  // item-replicate interaction effect

    // Priors for fixed component.
    alpha ~ normal(0, 10000);
   
    // Priors for variance components.
    gamma    ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
    sigma[1] ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
    sigma[2] ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
    tau      ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
    omega    ~ gamma(2, 0.1);

    // Distributions of random effects.
    u_raw ~ normal(0, 1);
    u <- gamma * u_raw;    

    for (i in 1:n_meth) {
        c_raw[i] ~ normal(0, 1);
        c[i] <- tau * c_raw[i];  
    }

    for (i in 1:n_factor) {
        a_raw[i] ~ normal(0, 1);
        a[i] <- omega * a_raw[i];
    }

    // Distribution of the outcome variable.
    for (n in 1:n_all) {
        y[n] ~ normal(alpha[meth[n]] +
                          u[item[n]] +
                      a[repl_ind[n]] +
                 c[meth[n], item[n]],
                      sigma[meth[n]]);
    }

}


generated quantities {
 
  real<lower=0> sigmaRatio;
  real alphaDiff;
 
  sigmaRatio <- sigma[1]/sigma[2];
  alphaDiff  <- alpha[1]-alpha[2];
 
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Strange behaviour of scale parameters in a linear mixed-effects model
parts:
I'm not really an expert on any of this, but all
of these parameters can be problematic:

> // Priors for fixed component.
> alpha ~ normal(0, 10000);
>
> // Priors for variance components.
> gamma ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
> sigma[1] ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
> sigma[2] ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
> tau ~ gamma(2, 0.1);
> omega ~ gamma(2, 0.1);

It's best to have the parameters not only non-centered, but
on the unit scale. Non-centering involves both the
location and scale of the normal, so if you insist on these
very wide priors, what you want to do is take

alpha_raw ~ normal(0, 1);

alpha = alpha_raw * 10000;

The gammas with paramters less than 1 can be bad news as
Andrew keeps pointing out. He has papers on this and there
are pointers in the manual.

Also, you don't have priors at all on parameters like c_raw.
Was that intentional?

- Bob
